text:
For a grounded conducting sphere the method of images gives an image charge  

\[
q'=-\,q\frac{R}{d}
\]

located on the line joining the real charge to the centre at a distance  

\[
a=\frac{R^{2}}{d}
\]

from the centre (inside the sphere).

The interaction energy of the real charge with the induced charge distribution is half the product of the real charge and the potential at its position due to the image charge:

\[
U=\frac12 q\,V_{\text{image}}(d)
\]

The distance between the real charge (at \(d\)) and the image charge (at \(a\)) is  

\[
d-a = d-\frac{R^{2}}{d}= \frac{d^{2}-R^{2}}{d}.
\]

Hence  

\[
V_{\text{image}}(d)=k\frac{q'}{d-a}=k\frac{-qR/d}{(d^{2}-R^{2})/d}
      =-k\frac{qR}{d^{2}-R^{2}} .
\]

Therefore  

\[
U=\frac12 q\left(-k\frac{qR}{d^{2}-R^{2}}\right)
   =-\frac12\,k\,\frac{q^{2}R}{d^{2}-R^{2}} .
\]

So the net potential energy of the system is  

\[
\boxed{U=-\frac12\,k\,\frac{q^{2}R}{d^{2}-R^{2}} }.
\]

This matches option **(D)**.  

Answer: D.
